newsitem.title: JAPAN: No fresh Iraqi barrels offered to Japan - traders.
newsitem.headline: No fresh Iraqi barrels offered to Japan - traders.

text.p: Iraq has not offered to sell extra crude oil on the Asian spot market and would be unlikely to find much interest among buyers in any case, Japanese traders said on Friday.
Japanese companies have mostly covered their requirements for March-lifting cargoes, and it would be difficult for them to make arrangements to buy any more prompt cargoes, traders said.
Many traders also said it would be difficult, although not impossible, to arrange shipping schedules to lift the crude at this late date.

Iraq is seeking to sell crude oil on a spot basis to make up for a shortfall in revenue from an oil-for-food plan, which has been caused by a decline in global crude oil prices. The extra cargoes would have to be lifted by March 9
"We haven"t heard anything from Iraq," one trader with a leading Japanese oil company said.
"I think it will be difficult for most Japanese companies to buy from Iraq now," he added.
Under the terms of an oil-for-food deal, Iraq can sell $1 billion worth of crude oil from December 10 to March 9, and another $1 billion during a second 90-day period.

Iraq has signed term contracts to sell the crude oil, but recent declines in global crude prices has meant extra cargo availability. A report filed last week at the U.N. Iraq sanctions committee put the total value of the first three month's worth of contracts at about $800 million.
The United Nations is expected to allow Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) to make up any shortfall by selling additional oil on the spot market.
Some Japanese traders said there was a possibility SOMO would contact them about spot sales.
In a separate development, a few traders said some Iraqi crude oil purchased under a term contract by Russian state oil holding company Rosneft had been offered for sale to Japanese companies.
"It hasn't been offered to us directly from the Russian company, but when we asked about who held the crude, the answer was Rosneft," a trader with a large Japanese oil company said.
Japanese companies said they had no interest in Iraqi crude offered by the Russian company, however.
Russian companies have been slow to lift their contracted volumes.
On the other hand, a trader with another major Japanese oil company said that some firms might consider making purchases from Iraq.

He said the purpose of the purchase would be to maintain close ties with SOMO, which was an important crude oil exporter to Japan before sanctions were imposed against Baghdad for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
"(If purchases were made) it would be a strategic step, rather than based on any real physical demand for the crude," the trader said.
Mitsubishi Corp, acting for five Japanese oil companies, has signed a contract to buy 20,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Iraq"s Basrah Light crude over a period of six months.
The Japanese trading firm was forced to accept a reduction in volume from an initial 40,000 barrels bpd over three months at SOMO's request.
